title: Know what to look for
summary: Spot food choices that support your goal in the places you actually eat.

overview_video.label: Overview video
overview_video.title: Know what to look for
overview_video.summary: Short intro to spotting goal-supportive food choices in dining halls, restaurants, grocery stores, meals someone else prepares, and food you make at home. The central message is "Look for the clue before you choose." Highlights saturated fat, sodium, added sugars, and fiber as useful cues depending on your focus.

cafeteria.label: Cafeteria or dining hall
cafeteria.prompt_template: You're grabbing {meal_period} at {dining_hall}. Here are three options. Let's take a look at their labels and pick one.

follow_up.prompt: Which did you look at first?

practical_suggestions.saturated_fat_g: Smaller portion of the item highest in saturated fat, or pair it with a vegetable side.
practical_suggestions.sodium_mg: Ask for sauce or dressing on the side when you can, and round out the plate with fruit or vegetables.
practical_suggestions.fiber_g: Add a side of fruit, beans, or vegetables for more fiber.

restaurant.label: Restaurant or takeout
restaurant.prompt: You're out for dinner with friends and ordering from the menu. Which would you go for?

choices.feedback: DRAFT — Grilled is a useful menu clue: it usually means less added fat than fried or crispy. The fries are the sodium and saturated-fat side of this choice, so a swap or share is worth asking about. One ask that often works: 'Can I get a side salad or fruit instead of fries?'

choices.text: Roasted salmon with steamed vegetables and rice
choices.feedback: DRAFT — Roasted, steamed, and salmon are all strong menu clues: unsaturated fats from the fish, cooking methods without added fat, and vegetables you can see on the plate. If the rice is white, you could ask whether brown rice is available.

choices.text: Crispy chicken wrap with a side salad
choices.feedback: DRAFT — Crispy on a menu usually means fried, which adds saturated fat and sometimes sodium. The side salad is a strong move for fiber and vegetables. If you want to lean further into the wrap, ask whether grilled chicken is available instead of crispy.

follow_up.prompt: Which menu word did you notice first?

grocery.label: Grocery or convenience store
grocery.prompt_template: You're picking up {category_label_lower} for the week. Here are three options. Let's check the labels.

follow_up.prompt: Which part of the label did you check first?

practical_suggestions.saturated_fat_g: If two products are similar on serving size, picking the one lower in saturated fat is an easy win.
practical_suggestions.sodium_mg: A difference of a few hundred milligrams of sodium adds up across meals; the lower-sodium pick carries more flexibility for the rest of the day.
practical_suggestions.added_sugars_g: Lower added sugars at the start of the day leaves room for a treat later without going over.
practical_suggestions.fiber_g: A couple more grams of fiber per serving is a strong vote for a product you'll reach for again.

someone_else.label: A meal someone else prepares
someone_else.prompt: You're at a family dinner, or a friend's place, and the food is set out. You're filling your plate.

choices.text: Fried chicken and mac and cheese
choices.feedback: DRAFT — These are familiar comfort foods. If this is what's on the table, you can enjoy it and still keep your goal in play — a smaller spoon of the mac, or saving room for whatever vegetable is in reach. There's no need to swap out foods that matter to the people you're with.

choices.text: Grilled chicken, rice and beans, and a salad
choices.feedback: DRAFT — Lots to work with: a lean protein, beans for fiber, a vegetable side. Rice and beans together are a classic combination that stretches both into something more filling. If dressing is on the salad, asking for it on the side is an easy ask when you can.

choices.text: A little of everything, with seconds on the vegetables
choices.feedback: DRAFT — A plate that samples what's served honors the host and still leaves room for your goal — the "seconds on vegetables" move is a quietly strong one and nobody has to notice. You get to enjoy the meal and still support what you're working on.

home.label: At home
home.prompt: You're making dinner at home with a can of beans, rice, and some vegetables. You have about 20 minutes.

choices.text: Beans straight from the can with the liquid, over white rice
choices.feedback: DRAFT — Fast and filling. The canned bean liquid usually carries a lot of sodium — a quick rinse in a colander takes about 30 seconds and makes a real difference without changing the meal. White rice works; whole-grain brown rice would add more fiber if you have it on hand next time.

choices.text: Rinsed beans with vegetables and brown rice
choices.feedback: DRAFT — Strong move. Rinsing the beans cuts a chunk of the sodium, the vegetables add fiber and bulk, and brown rice brings whole grains into the plate. This is a weeknight staple worth having in rotation.

choices.text: Beans and vegetables with cheese, over white rice
choices.feedback: DRAFT — The vegetables and beans are a strong foundation. Cheese adds flavor and some saturated fat; a smaller handful goes a long way when it's melted on top. If you reach for brown rice next time, you'll also pick up more fiber.

planning.label: Plan where you'll use it
planning.title: Planning where you'll use it
planning.intro: Here's your plan from last week. This week you practiced spotting better choices. Now, pick a moment to use it.

p1_moment.prompt: Pick one eating situation coming up this week where you can use what you practiced.

p2_action.prompt: What will you look for or choose there?

p3_barrier.prompt: What's one thing that could make this harder?

p4_coping.prompt: If that happens, what will you do?

p5_plan_management.prompt: What do you want to do with last week's plan?

options.label: Keep last week's plan and add this one.
Replace last week's plan with this one.

p5_plan_management.reminder_prompt: What's a good time for a reminder?
p5_plan_management.reminder_note: Default is one hour before the eating moment. You can change it.

planning.completion_summary_template: Thanks. Here's your plan: When {situation_and_time}, you'll {action}. If {barrier}, you'll {coping}. We'll remind you {reminder_time}. You can change it any time.
planning.completion_summary_keep_only_template: Thanks. You kept last week's plan. We saved your Week 2 answers, but they're on hold — change your mind any time.
